chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his forefathers (peace be upon them):

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) passed by a man planting a plant in a walled garden of his. So he stopped before him and said: Shall I not guide you to a plant with firmer roots, quicker ripening, sweeter fruits, and more lasting produce? He said: Of course — may my father and mother be your sacrifice, O Messenger of God. So he said: When you awake in the morning and when you reach the evening, say: Glory be to God, and all praise belongs to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the greatest. For indeed, if you say that, with each glorification you will have ten trees in Paradise of various kinds of fruit, and they are from the everlasting good deeds.
He said: The man then said: I bear you witness, O Messenger of God, that this walled garden of mine is a charity given to the poor Muslims from the people of al-Suffah.
So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: As for he who gives and fears God and testifies to goodness, We shall surely ease his way toward bliss. (92:5-7)

key_terms.أهل الصفة: The People of al-Suffah — poor Companions who resided on the covered porch of the Prophet's Mosque in Medina
key_terms.الباقيات الصالحات: The everlasting good deeds — a Quranic term (18:46, 19:76) referring to dhikr and righteous acts that endure
key_terms.تسبيحة: A single utterance of glorification (tasbeeh) — specifically saying 'Subhanallah'
key_terms.غرس: Plant/planting — used metaphorically for spiritual deeds whose fruits are reaped in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the reward of dhikr compared to planting trees?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) encountered a man planting trees in his garden and offered him something better: the dhikr of 'Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar,' which earns ten heavenly trees per recitation. This teaching, delivered to an ordinary gardener in Medina, uses a powerful agricultural metaphor that the audience — mostly farmers — would have immediately understood. The man's response of donating his entire garden to the poor Muslims of al-Suffah (the destitute Companions who lived on the porch of the Prophet's mosque) was so exemplary that God revealed Quran 92:5-7 in his honor.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham b. Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Malik b. `Atiyya from Durays al-Kinasi from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir from his forefathers (as).

The Messenger of Allah (s) passed by a man planting a plant in a wall of his. So, he went to him and said: Shall I not lead you to a plant with the firmest roots, the quickest ripening, the sweetest fruits, and the longest-lasting produce? He said: Of course – may my father and my mother be your sacrifice, O Messenger of Allah. So, he said: When you awake and when you go to sleep, say “may Allah be glorified, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the greatest” (subhanallah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha ilallah, wallahu akbar).” If you say that, with each glorification you will have ten trees in Paradise with a variety of fruits – these are from the everlasting, goodly things.
He said: So, the man said: I bear you witness, O Messenger of Allah. This wall of mine is a charity given to the poor Muslims of the Ahl al-Suffah.
So, Allah revealed, “He who gives and fears and testifies to goodness, We shall surely ease his way to bliss.” (92:5-7)
